The high catalyst run is now beginning to differentiate. M17, M12, M14, M20, M11, M9 are top (all around -57.5). Meanwhile M1, M19, M8, M6, M7 trail at -55 to -56. M4, M5 clearly worse. 

Interestingly the top mechanisms include several deactivation (M9, M14, M20, M11) and product inhibition (M12, M17) mechanisms. Simple M1 and reversible mechanisms are falling behind. This suggests some form of catalyst loss or product inhibition is happening.

To discriminate:
- Product inhibition (M12, M17) vs deactivation (M9, M11, M14, M20): using high P again plus low cat would amplify these. But I already did P=0.3.
- Low catalyst + long time: deactivation effects become pronounced; M9 has 1st order in cat deactivation, M13/M18 are 2nd order
- High substrate: M11 (S-induced deactivation) and M16 distinguish themselves
</reflection>

Use a high substrate, low catalyst experiment. Low catalyst amplifies deactivation (turnover-limited), and high S distinguishes mechanisms with S-dependent deactivation (M11, M16) vs. pure deactivation (M9, M14, M20), vs. product inhibition (M12, M17).

Also, a low catalyst run generates a long kinetic trace with slower progression, revealing more curvature differences. At S=3.0, cat=0.002, P=0, we get a very different turnover regime than previous runs.
</hypothesis>
